territorial_scope.description: California state statute; the enacting clause places it within state law, with no operative geographic limit stated in the provisions.

evidence.quote: The people of the State of California do enact as follows:

summary.short: Prohibits distributing, with actual malice, materially deceptive audio or visual media of a candidate within 60 days of an election, unless it carries a manipulation disclosure; gives candidates injunctive relief and damages; the new provision is repealed 1 January 2023 unless extended.
summary.long: Adds Elections Code Sec. 20010 (subds. a-g). Within 60 days of an election in which a candidate for elective office appears on the ballot, a person, committee or other entity may not distribute, with actual malice and intent to injure the candidate's reputation or deceive a voter, materially deceptive audio or visual media of the candidate. Such media are intentionally manipulated so as to falsely appear authentic and to convey a fundamentally different impression of their expressive content. The ban does not apply if the media carries a 'has been manipulated' disclosure meeting size, duration or audio-reading rules. A candidate may seek injunctive relief, with precedence under Code of Civil Procedure Sec. 35, and sue for general or special damages and fees, proving violation by clear and convincing evidence. Exemptions cover paid broadcasts, bona fide news coverage acknowledging authenticity questions, websites or periodicals stating the media does not accurately represent the candidate, and satire or parody. Rights, obligations and immunities of interactive service providers under 47 U.S.C. Sec. 230 are not altered. Other sections amend Sec. 20010 on superimposed candidate images, operative 1 January 2023, and Code of Civil Procedure Sec. 35 on election-case precedence. The new Sec. 20010 text is in effect only until 1 January 2023, unless a later statute extends it.

notes: Chaptered text, annotated as the enacted session law. Two versions each of CCP § 35 and Elections Code § 20010 appear: the amended versions (Sec. 1, Sec. 3) and the added versions (Sec. 2, Sec. 4) carry different operative or sunset dates, all tied to 1 January 2023. The repeal of the amended § 35 and the sunset of the added § 20010 operate through their own subdivisions ((b) and (g)); no separate repeal provision appears. The registry status is in_force; the text sets a 1 January 2023 sunset, which this annotation does not evaluate.
